<skill_instructions>
# Word documents

Use `python-docx` for DOCX creation and ordinary edits. Follow an explicit user or applicable AGENTS.md requirement for a project environment or another library. Otherwise call `load_workspace_dependencies` and execute the returned Python path with its bundled libraries. Do not install packages or discover a system Python for the default workflow. If the tool is unavailable, use an already configured environment and report a missing dependency only when it prevents the requested operation.

Keep source scripts, intermediate files, and final documents in the task workspace; the runtime and this skill directory are read-only resources. Use the user's requested language and preserve an existing document's design unless a redesign is requested.

Name Python scripts for their task, such as `edit_docx.py`; avoid module names such as `inspect.py`, `docx.py`, or `zipfile.py` that shadow imported libraries.

## Create and edit

For text edits, locate the target by its text or position and inspect only its runs and formatting. A title can be an ordinary paragraph without a Title style or document-property title. Update the relevant runs; assigning paragraph `.text` destroys run formatting. Save a new file unless an in-place edit is requested. For ordinary text edits, do not unzip the document, enumerate ZIP members, dump raw XML, or inspect core properties, headers, or footers unrelated to the target. Investigate these only for a concrete failure, an ambiguous target, an unsupported feature, or an explicit user requirement. Rebuilding a document can lose unsupported features.

Use paragraph styles for headings and body text. Size tables for the section that contains them, and account for merged cells and nested tables. Chinese, Japanese, and Korean text may need an explicit `w:eastAsia` font assignment in addition to `run.font.name`; font names alone do not establish glyph availability or rendered appearance.

For a new document, use the selected Python executable:

```python
from docx import Document

document = Document()
document.add_heading("Project report", level=0)
document.add_paragraph("Summary", style="Heading 1")
document.add_paragraph("The requested findings go here.")
document.save("report.docx")
```

python-docx does not paginate or render documents. Do not represent ordinary replacement, colored text, or comments as tracked changes. When real revisions or unsupported OOXML features matter, preserve their package parts and verify the requested operation rather than silently discarding them. When writing package parts directly, create a new ZIP and copy each unchanged member once; appending a replacement member duplicates its name and corrupts the package.

## Check and deliver

Reopen the saved document with python-docx and verify the requested content, related formatting, and unchanged content that must be preserved. When these checks pass, stop validation and deliver the file. Do not add ZIP integrity checks, package inventories, or metadata inspection as routine final verification.

Creating a file or changing content with incidental basic formatting does not require additional operations. Load `office-render` for requested images or visual inspection. When styling, font color, spacing, sizing, or text alignment is the requested edit, load `office-render` and inspect the changed page even without a separate visual-check request, unless the user explicitly skips rendering. For PDF output load `office-export-pdf`.

Call `present({"files":[{"path":"report.docx"}]})` with the actual final DOCX path. It exposes the current source file without copying or preserving its bytes, so keep that file in place and do not present temporary QA reports unless requested. If `present` is unavailable, provide the final workspace path using the session's supported file delivery method.
</skill_instructions>
</skill_content>

<skill_instructions>
# Document images and visual inspection

Use the installed LibreOffice Kit CLI through the shell with the absolute Node and CLI paths supplied below. In Bash, invoke `"<node>" "<cli>"`; in PowerShell, invoke `& "<node>" "<cli>"`. Prefer bundled LibreOffice unless the user requests another installation. If the Office sidecar is missing, follow [sidecar setup](../office/references/sidecar.md): ask whether the user wants to download it and install only after they agree. Do not invoke system soffice, use npx, install a replacement renderer, or build an alternative rendering pipeline to work around a failed render with an installed sidecar.

Before generating images only for inspection, establish that the current model accepts images. Otherwise finish the applicable content and structure checks and report the requested visual check as unavailable. Do not generate unreadable previews, retry image reads, or choose a second model. Requested image exports can still be delivered.

## Render the saved deliverable

Keep the saved deliverable in the task workspace. For requested image exports, use the requested output directory and retain the images. For inspection-only previews, create a private, uniquely named temporary parent inside that workspace and pass a child path that does not yet exist as `--output-dir`; the CLI creates that child. On POSIX, use `preview_root=$(mktemp -d "./.dsh-office.XXXXXXXX")` (owner-only permissions) and `--output-dir "$preview_root/render"`. On PowerShell, create a parent named `.dsh-office-` plus `[guid]::NewGuid().ToString('N')` under the task workspace and pass an uncreated `render` child; it inherits the workspace ACL. Quote each input and output path. Retain the parent until image inspection finishes, then remove only that parent, including after a failed render. Never use a fixed directory name or remove the workspace itself. Report inspection results in text; the reply must not link or embed removed previews.

```text
"<node>" "<cli>" render --input <final-file> --output-dir <new-directory> --pages "1,3,4"
"<node>" "<cli>" render --input <final-workbook.xlsx> --output-dir <new-directory> --sheet <exact-name> --range <A1-range>
```

For DOCX, PPTX, or PDF, batch requested pages/slides in one call. In PowerShell, quote comma-separated `--pages` values so they remain one argument. Inspect all pages only for a requested whole-document review. For worksheets, choose the exact affected range, including chart/drawing regions; worksheet numbers are not PDF page numbers. Inspect the final saved file, reuse existing images for an unchanged source, and rerender only after requested source changes or for previously unrendered regions. Change print areas or scaling only when the user requests print layout.

Read the returned JSON manifest for image paths, page counts, fragment rectangles, and missing-font diagnostics. Use the session's image-reading tool to inspect the requested images. Check clipping, alignment, headings, table widths, contrast, chart labels, and number formats as relevant to the task. A successful command or image read alone does not establish a usable preview; guessed text geometry does not establish overflow.

## Failed or blank previews

For populated content, a fully transparent or uniformly blank image is a renderer failure. If a pixel check is needed, composite RGBA onto white first; raw RGB under transparent pixels can look nonblank. Check once and do not reread the same image. Stop visual checks for the task immediately after a blank result. This overrides the rerender-after-edit guidance above: do not render or read images again, even after editing or copying the source, or try another range, page, sheet, DPI, output format, diagnostic export, or print setting. Preserve the usable source and requested outputs and finish applicable content/data checks.

If content and structure checks pass, name the saved file and verified edits as needed, then include exactly one visual-status sentence: "Content and structure checks passed; visual inspection was not completed." in English, or "内容与结构检查通过；视觉检查未完成。" in Chinese. Do not add a render or preview bullet, explain why inspection stopped, or describe the image or pixels. Report content or structure failures separately; never say all checks passed or claim visual verification.

LibreOffice output can differ from Word, PowerPoint, or Excel. Images do not certify animation/media playback, refresh formula caches in the source workbook, or guarantee native application fidelity. Deliver requested files through `present` when available; keep the files in place. Do not deliver inspection images or reports unless requested.

## Installed LibreOffice Kit

Use these absolute paths for every LibreOffice Kit command. Pass the CLI entry as the first argument to Node.

{
  "libreofficeKit": {
    "node": "{{cwd}}/office-node",
    "cli": "{{cwd}}/render-cli.cjs"
  }
}
</skill_instructions>
</skill_content>

# Export an Office document to PDF

Use the installed LibreOffice Kit CLI through the shell with the absolute Node and CLI paths supplied below. In Bash, invoke `"<node>" "<cli>"`; in PowerShell, invoke `& "<node>" "<cli>"`. Prefer bundled LibreOffice unless the user requests another installation. If the Office sidecar is missing, follow [sidecar setup](../office/references/sidecar.md): ask whether the user wants to download it and install only after they agree. Do not invoke system soffice, use npx, or install a replacement to work around a failed conversion with an installed sidecar.

Convert the final saved Office file to a new PDF in the task workspace. Preserve the source. Quote each input and output path.

```text
"<node>" "<cli>" convert --input <final-office-file> --output <new-file.pdf>
```

Check the command result, nonempty output, and `%PDF-` file signature, then report that extent of validation. Unless the user requests deeper checks, do not search for PDF readers, generate images, or install tools to validate a conversion. Spreadsheet PDF pages follow workbook print settings; change those settings only when requested. Conversion may differ from the native application's pagination or fonts.

If export fails, preserve the usable source and report the export limitation. Do not repeatedly convert an unchanged source or use conversion to investigate a failed preview. For PDF export alone, stop after these checks. Only a request for images or visual inspection calls for `office-render`; load it before that separate operation. Deliver the requested PDF through `present` when available, keeping the file in place.

## Installed LibreOffice Kit

Use these absolute paths for every LibreOffice Kit command. Pass the CLI entry as the first argument to Node.

{
  "libreofficeKit": {
    "node": "{{cwd}}/office-node",
    "cli": "{{cwd}}/render-cli.cjs"
  }
}
</skill_instructions>
</skill_content>
